newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine air force to buy 12 fighter jets.
newsitem.headline: Philippine air force to buy 12 fighter jets.

text.p: The Philippine Air Force has proposed to buy up to 12 fighter jets and radar equipment this year to fortify the country's air defence system, Air Force chief Lieutenant General William Hotchkiss said on Friday.
"There is an intent to do that but it will depend on the national leadership to get it off budget," Hotchkiss told a news conference ahead of the air force's 50th anniversary.
Hotchkiss said suppliers from South Korea, Taiwan, Canada and Singapore had offered to supply either refurbished or new fighter jets to Manila.
The purchase of a squadron of fighter jets and air defence radar equipment are necessary to boost the Philippine's air defence capabilities.
The Air Force has a fleet of 298 planes, of which 150 are operational, including five F-5s and four C-130s.
The Philippines also has one radar system, covering at least 10 percent of the country's total air space.
Hotchkiss said the Air Force's proposal to purchase an initial 12 fighter jets and radar equipment was separate from the $2 billion modernisation programme of the Philippine armed forces.
The Air Force is presently evaluating proposals for the supply of fighter jets from the United States, Israel, France, Russia and Sweden, he said.
Suppliers from Spain, Italy, United States and Israel have also offered to supply 46 air defence radar sets, he added.
The Air Force will submit the short-list of bidders by the end of this month to Defence Secretary Renato de Villa, Hotchkiss said.

Armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera said recently the Philippines was shopping for 24 second-hand fighter jets and a dozen naval vessels. Among the planes Manila was looking at were U.S.-made F-16s and Russian-made MIG-29s, he said.

Recent disputes between the Philippines and China over ownership of islands in and near the Spratlys in the South China Sea have prompted Philippine congressional leaders to urge Manila to speed up the modernisation programme.

"We would like to get multi-role fighters and air defence radar so we can come up with a credible air defence system where we can detect, identify intrusions and possibly intercept them," Hotchkiss said.
